chunks: Sa'd narrated from Abu Ja'far, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah, who said: Abu al-Qasim Mu'awiya narrated to me from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Samma, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He said to me: In the Qunut of Witr (prayer), [say]: 'O Allah, forgive us and have mercy on us, grant us well-being and pardon us in this world and the Hereafter.' And he said: 'Three glorifications (Tasbihat) suffice for the Qunut.'

key_terms.اللَّهُمَّ اغْفِرْ لَنَا: O Allah, forgive us (opening of the supplication)
key_terms.ثَلَاثُ تَسْبِيحَاتٍ: Three glorifications (referring to saying Subhanallah three times)
key_terms.قُنُوتِ الْوَتْرِ: Qunut of Witr (supplication in the Witr prayer)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication and minimum recitation for the Qunut in Witr prayer according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) specifies a concise supplication for the Qunut of Witr, emphasizing divine mercy and well-being in both the worldly and hereafter realms, while establishing that three glorifications suffice to fulfill this recommended act. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle of ease in supererogatory acts, distinguishing the sufficiency of Tasbihat from the recitation of longer supplications found in other traditions. The emphasis on 'well-being' (Afā) aligns with the holistic spiritual and physical health sought in Shia devotional practices.
